harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built the lan-a/lan-b topology on node1 (OPNsense) using its two spare interfaces (vtnet1=opt1/lan-a 10.50.10.1/24, vtnet2=opt2/lan-b 10.50.20.1/24), addressed node2's enp8s0 (10.50.10.11/24, lan-a) and node3's enp8s0 (10.50.20.12/24, lan-b) via NetworkManager persistent profiles, added cross-subnet static routes on node2/node3 via node1, and added firewall pass rules for opt1/opt2 plus a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule (source 10.50.10.0/24, interface opt2, target=interface address) so node2->node3 traffic is source-NATed to node1's opt2 address 10.50.20.1 while node3->node2 traffic keeps its original source. Verified via tcpdump on node3's and node2's LAN interfaces during live TCP sessions. Then executed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node2, node3, node1), confirming boot-identity changes (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) and re-verifying interface config, firewall/NAT rules, routing, and the asymmetric-NAT behavior end-to-end after all restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) config.xml, interfaces vtnet0/1/2, and node2/node3 NIC layout (enp1s0 mgmt, enp8s0 spare)
Assigned static IPs 10.50.10.11/24 (node2) and 10.50.20.12/24 (node3) to enp8s0 via nmcli persistent profiles after discovering NetworkManager reclaimed manual `ip addr` changes
Added OPNsense interfaces opt1 (vtnet1, 10.50.10.1/24, lan-a) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.50.20.1/24, lan-b) by editing /conf/config.xml and reloading via configctl interface reconfigure
Added firewall pass rules for opt1 and opt2 networks and reloaded pf via configctl filter reload
Configured hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule on node1: source 10.50.10.0/24 exiting opt2 -> translated to opt2 interface address (10.50.20.1), leaving opt1-bound (reverse) traffic untranslated
Added static routes on node2 (10.50.20.0/24 via 10.50.10.1) and node3 (10.50.10.0/24 via 10.50.20.1) via nmcli
Opened firewalld ports and ran socat listeners/clients plus tcpdump captures on node2 and node3 to confirm forward NAT and reverse non-NAT behavior
Captured pre-restart baseline boot identity and health (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id/uptime on node2/node3, interface/NAT/route state)
Sequentially rebooted node2, node3, then node1 (router last), polling each until exec was available again
Confirmed changed boot identity for each node (differing boot_id for node2/node3, differing kern.boottime for node1)
Re-verified interface addresses, firewall rules, NAT rules, and routes persisted post-reboot on all three nodes
Re-ran an end-to-end socat/tcpdump test after all restarts confirming node2->node3 traffic still arrives as 10.50.20.1 (NATed)

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
evidence.summary: opt1/opt2 interfaces up with correct IPs, node2 and node3 can ping node1's respective interfaces and each other's subnet across node1

evidence.requirement: node2->node3 connection observed by node3 as arriving from a node1 address, not node2's own address
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node3's enp8s0 during a live TCP session from node2 shows the connection sourced from 10.50.20.1 (node1's lan-b/opt2 address), not node2's real address 10.50.10.11

evidence.requirement: reverse direction (node3->node2) keeps original source address
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node2's enp8s0 during a live TCP session from node3 shows the connection sourced from node3's real address 10.50.20.12, unmodified

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bf8b9d80...; reboot acknowledged in background; new boot_id f8f8ec35... confirms restart; enp8s0 IP/route and ping to node1 recovered post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 71f12f87...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 04122c48... confirms restart; enp8s0 IP/route and ping to node1 recovered post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 (router) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime sec=1788627139; reboot acknowledged in background; new kern.boottime sec=1788627781 confirms restart; opt1/opt2 interfaces, firewall pass rules, and NAT rule all persisted and reloaded correctly post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Asymmetric NAT behavior persists after all three node restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart end-to-end test: node2->node3 TCP connection still observed by node3 as arriving from node1's opt2 address 10.50.20.1, confirming durability of the configuration
